body.statement: If \(z\) is induced by an observed law \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), then \(\psi(z)=(a,q_0,q_1,e_0,e_1,p_0,p_1)\), \(\widetilde f_\beta^s(z)=f_\beta^s(P)\) for every \(s\in\{-,+\}\) and \(\beta\in\{0,1\}^6\), and \(\widetilde F_s(z)=F_s(P)\) for both signs. In particular, \(\widetilde F_+(z)=\widetilde f_\beta^+(z)\) for every \(\beta\in\mathcal B_+(P)\), and \(\widetilde F_-(z)=\widetilde f_\beta^-(z)\) for every \(\beta\in\mathcal B_-(P)\), including all active ties.
body.justification: The cell factorizations \(z_{\ell\mathrm N}=a q_\ell(1-e_\ell)\) and \(z_{\ell y}=a q_\ell e_\ell p_\ell^y(1-p_\ell)^{1-y}\) recover every primitive coordinate, so direct substitution identifies the simplex and law-indexed formulas.
body.gap: Tan (2025) indexes the endpoint by the observed law but does not give a seven-cell simplex extension for every binary rational branch.
body.consumer: It makes the empirical plug-in map and every gradient in the multiplier envelope functions of the same multinomial probability vector.
body.proof_tex:
For a law \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), the seven cell probabilities factor as
\[
 z_\varnothing=1-a,\qquad
 z_{\ell\mathrm N}=a q_\ell(1-e_\ell),\qquad
 z_{\ell y}=a q_\ell e_\ell p_\ell^y(1-p_\ell)^{1-y}.
\]
Every factor is positive by \(\mathrm{ass{:}eta\text{-}interior}\).  Hence
\[
 d_\ell=z_{\ell\mathrm N}+z_{\ell0}+z_{\ell1}=a q_\ell,\qquad
 m_\ell=z_{\ell0}+z_{\ell1}=a q_\ell e_\ell,\qquad
 z_{\ell1}=a q_\ell e_\ell p_\ell.
\]
The coordinate definitions therefore give
\[
 a(z)=a,\quad q_\ell(z)=q_\ell,\quad e_\ell(z)=e_\ell,\quad p_\ell(z)=p_\ell,
\]
which proves the asserted identity for \(\psi(z)\).  Direct substitution of these seven equalities into every formula in \(\mathrm{def{:}seven\text{-}cell\text{-}simplex\text{-}extensions}\) gives, successively,
\[
 \widetilde r_{\ell\beta}^s(z)=r_{\ell\beta}^s,\quad
 \widetilde t_{\ell\beta}^s(z)=t_{\ell\beta}^s,\quad
 \widetilde h_\beta(z)=h_\beta,\quad
 \widetilde f_\beta^s(z)=f_\beta^s(P).
\]
The same substitution in the compact envelope formulas yields \(\widetilde F_s(z)=F_s(P)\).  Finally, the sharp-frontier theorem and the weak branch rules imply equality with every branch in \(\mathcal B_s(P)\).  Because tied affine pieces agree at their common face and the final expression is independent of \(h\) when its two stratum values tie, this conclusion includes every active tie.
